input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The new minimum wait defaults to one second instead of zero.
- failure path: With default options, an early exponential result below one second is raised to a one-second delay, slowing retries that previously had no configured floor.

Reviewer finding
- description: Defaulting the new minimum to 1 changes existing subsecond backoff configurations and can make waits exceed the configured maximum. Defaulting it to 0 would preserve existing behavior unless callers explicitly request a minimum.
- rationale: For an existing configuration such as wait_exponential_jitter(initial=0.1, max=0.5, jitter=0), callers omit the newly added min argument. It now defaults to 1, so the outer max in __call__ returns 1 on every attempt instead of waits between 0.1 and 0.5 seconds, slowing retries and exceeding the caller's configured maximum.
critique: The finding names the same root cause: the new min parameter defaults to 1 instead of 0. It also describes the same failure: subsecond exponential waits get raised to one second when callers omit min, which slows retries. The extra point about exceeding max is a consequence of the same mechanism.
